traps: Profit fell while revenue grew 28%: operating income down 8%, net income down 14%, diluted EPS down 13%, operating margin 31% vs 43%; a brief that implies earnings growth misstates the quarter.

Meta reports no adjusted EPS or adjusted net income; its only non-GAAP measures are revenue excluding foreign exchange effect and free cash flow, so any EPS excluding the legal or severance charges is not company-reported.
Reported revenue growth is 28% (GAAP); 27% is constant currency. Advertising revenue grew 27% GAAP and 26% excluding foreign exchange.

Quarter vs six months: six-month columns show net income of $42,621 million and diluted EPS of $16.62, both up year over year because of a six-month income tax benefit of $2,113 million; they are not the quarter.
The $2.40 billion legal charges and $1.18 billion severance are inside GAAP costs, margin and EPS; the legal charges sit in general and administrative expenses.

Three different outlook ranges: Q3 2026 revenue $61-64 billion, full year 2026 total expenses $165-169 billion (lower end raised), full year 2026 capex $130-145 billion (narrowed from $125-145 billion); mixing them up is easy.
Capital return was dividends only ($1.35 billion); the cash flow statement shows no Class A share repurchases in the quarter versus $10,167 million a year earlier, so do not report a buyback.
Capex of $31.08 billion includes principal payments on finance leases; purchases of property and equipment alone were $30,116 million.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $90.26 billion, but cash and cash equivalents alone were $15,462 million; long-term debt rose to $83.66 billion after $24,910 million of new debt issuance.
Units: tables are in millions; $23,394 million is about $23.4 billion, and free cash flow is $784 million, not billion.
Tax rate outlook for the remaining quarters of 2026 is 15-17%, up from a prior 13-16%; the Q2 effective tax rate was 16% vs 11%.
Operating income outlook is qualitative only (above 2025 operating income); no dollar figure is given.

The Q3 2026 revenue range of $61-64 billion assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth; a brief need not repeat the assumption, but it applies to revenue only, not to the expense or capex ranges.

Derived arithmetic is not accepted (prompts/t4.py rule 1; the judge marks a claim that needs a calculation unsupported): no computed FoA operating income decline (6.3%), margin change (12 points), free cash flow decline (about 91%), combined charges ($3.58 billion), guidance midpoint ($62.5 billion) or capex low-end raise ($5 billion); none is printed in the release.
